# SolidJS Documentation

Documentation for SolidJS, the signals-powered UI framework

- [Install and configure](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-meta/getting-started/installation-and-setup.md): Install and configure @solidjs/meta for head tag management. Set up dynamic titles, meta tags, and SEO optimization in Solid apps.
- [Client setup](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-meta/getting-started/client-setup.md): Manage document head tags in Solid apps. Add titles, meta tags, and links dynamically for better SEO and social media sharing.
- [Server setup](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-meta/getting-started/server-setup.md): Configure server-side rendering for Solid Meta tags with MetaProvider. Learn to properly inject head tags in SSR for optimal SEO and performance.
- [Overview](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-meta.md): Solid Meta provides asynchronous SSR-ready document head management. Define meta tags at any component level for flexible SEO and metadata control.
- [Base](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-meta/reference/meta/base.md): Base renders a base element through Solid Meta.
- [Link](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-meta/reference/meta/link.md): Link renders a link element through Solid Meta.
- [Meta](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-meta/reference/meta/meta.md): Meta renders a meta element through Solid Meta.
- [MetaProvider](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-meta/reference/meta/metaprovider.md): MetaProvider provides the context used by Solid Meta head tags.
- [Style](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-meta/reference/meta/style.md): Style renders a style element through Solid Meta.
- [Title](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-meta/reference/meta/title.md): Title renders a title element through Solid Meta.
- [useHead](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-meta/reference/meta/use-head.md): useHead adds a custom head tag through Solid Meta.
- [Installation and setup](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/getting-started/installation-and-setup.md): Learn how to install and configure Solid Router for client and server-side routing in your single-page applications with step-by-step setup guide.
- [Component routing](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/getting-started/component.md): Define routes using JSX components in SolidJS Router for intuitive, template-based routing in your applications.
- [Config-based routing](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/getting-started/config.md): Configure SolidJS routes with config objects for centralized routing, lazy loading, and optimized performance.
- [Linking routes](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/getting-started/linking-routes.md): Create navigation links between routes using anchor tags and the A component with active state styling and automatic base path handling.
- [Overview](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router.md): Solid Router is the universal routing solution for Solid applications, enabling client and server-side navigation in single-page applications.
- [Navigation](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/concepts/navigation.md): Navigate between routes in SolidJS using links, programmatic navigation, and redirects for seamless user experiences.
- [Path parameters](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/concepts/path-parameters.md): Capture and validate dynamic URL parameters in SolidJS routes for flexible content display and data-driven pages.
- [Search parameters](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/concepts/search-parameters.md): Manage query strings and search parameters in SolidJS for filtering, pagination, and maintaining state in the URL.
- [Catch-all routes](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/concepts/catch-all.md): Create catch-all routes in SolidJS to handle 404 errors and redirect users from invalid URLs to proper fallback pages.
- [Dynamic routes](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/concepts/dynamic-routes.md): Build dynamic routes with parameters in SolidJS for user profiles, products, and content that changes based on URL values.
- [Nesting routes](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/concepts/nesting.md): Build nested route hierarchies in SolidJS for complex applications with parent-child relationships and shared layouts.
- [Layouts](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/concepts/layouts.md): Create consistent page layouts in SolidJS with shared headers, footers, and nested structures for better UI organization.
- [Alternative routers](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/concepts/alternative-routers.md): Learn to use hash-based and memory routers in SolidJS for client-side navigation and testing without server interaction.
- [Actions](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/concepts/actions.md): Handle form submissions and server mutations with Solid Router actions. Build isomorphic data flows with progressive enhancement support.
- [Single page applications](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/rendering-modes/spa.md): Configure single-page applications for proper CDN and hosting deployment. Handle client-side routing without server-side rendering.
- [Server side rendering](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/rendering-modes/ssr.md): Enable server-side rendering with Solid Router for SEO and performance. Support suspense, resources, and render-as-you-fetch patterns.

- [useSubmission](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/data-apis/use-submission.md): useSubmission returns the latest tracked submission for an action.
- [useSubmissions](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/data-apis/use-submissions.md): useSubmissions returns tracked submissions for an action.

- [useIsRouting](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/primitives/use-is-routing.md): useIsRouting detects when a route transition is in progress.
- [useLocation](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/primitives/use-location.md): useLocation returns the current location.
- [useMatch](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/primitives/use-match.md): useMatch returns a memoized match for a path pattern.
- [useNavigate](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/primitives/use-navigate.md): useNavigate returns the navigation function.
- [useParams](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/primitives/use-params.md): useParams returns the current route parameters.
- [usePreloadRoute](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/primitives/use-preload-route.md): usePreloadRoute returns a function for preloading a route.
- [useResolvedPath](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/primitives/use-resolved-path.md): useResolvedPath returns an accessor for a path resolved against the current route.
- [useSearchParams](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/primitives/use-search-params.md): useSearchParams returns current query parameters and a query update function.
- [json](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/response-helpers/json.md): json returns a custom JSON response.
- [redirect](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/response-helpers/redirect.md): redirect returns a custom redirect response.
- [reload](https://docs.solidjs.com/solid-router/reference/response-helpers/reload.md): Reload and revalidate specific queries after mutations. Efficiently update cached data without full page refreshes for better UX.

## Overview

- [Overview](https://docs.solidjs.com/index.md): Solid is a reactive JavaScript framework for building fast, efficient UIs. Learn about fine-grained reactivity and modern web development.

## Concepts

### Components

- [Basics](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/components/basics.md): Learn Solid component fundamentals: creating reusable UI blocks, component trees, lifecycles, and proper import/export patterns.
- [Class and style](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/components/class-style.md): Style Solid components with CSS classes and inline styles. Learn dynamic styling, classList usage, and theme implementation.
- [Props](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/components/props.md): Pass and manage component props in Solid while maintaining reactivity. Learn mergeProps, splitProps, and best practices.
- [Event handlers](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/components/event-handlers.md): Handle user interactions in Solid with event delegation and native events for optimal performance and resource management.
- [Intro to reactivity](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/intro-to-reactivity.md): Master Solid's reactive system fundamentals: signals, subscribers, and automatic UI updates for responsive applications.

### Control Flow

- [Conditional rendering](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/control-flow/conditional-rendering.md): Conditionally render UI elements in Solid using Show, Switch, and Match components for clean, readable conditional logic.
- [List rendering](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/control-flow/list-rendering.md): Efficiently render dynamic lists in Solid using For and Index components. Optimize performance for different data scenarios.
- [Dynamic](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/control-flow/dynamic.md): Render components dynamically at runtime with Solid's Dynamic component. Build flexible UIs with runtime component selection.
- [Error boundary](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/control-flow/error-boundary.md): Catch and handle rendering errors gracefully with ErrorBoundary. Prevent app crashes and provide user-friendly error recovery.
- [Portal](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/control-flow/portal.md): Learn how Portal renders elements outside the normal DOM flow to solve z-index and overflow issues for modals and popups.
- [Understanding JSX](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/understanding-jsx.md): Write HTML-like syntax in JavaScript with JSX to create reactive components with dynamic expressions and event handlers.

### Derived Values

- [Derived signals](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/derived-values/derived-signals.md): Create reactive derived values that automatically update when their dependencies change using Solid's derived signals.
- [Memos](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/derived-values/memos.md): Optimize expensive computations with memos that cache results and only recalculate when dependencies actually change.
- [Signals](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/signals.md): Create reactive state with signals - the foundation of Solid's reactivity system for automatic UI updates and tracking.
- [Effects](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/effects.md): Manage side effects like DOM updates, API calls, and subscriptions that respond automatically to reactive state changes.
- [Context](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/context.md): Share data across component trees with Solid's Context API. Avoid prop drilling and manage global application state effectively.
- [Stores](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/stores.md): Manage complex nested state efficiently with stores that provide fine-grained reactivity for objects and arrays in Solid.
- [Refs](https://docs.solidjs.com/concepts/refs.md): Access and manipulate DOM elements directly using refs, forward refs between components, and create custom directives.

## Advanced Concepts

- [Fine-grained reactivity](https://docs.solidjs.com/advanced-concepts/fine-grained-reactivity.md): Master Solid's fine-grained reactivity system for targeted UI updates, optimal performance, and efficient state management patterns.

## Quick start

- [Quick start](https://docs.solidjs.com/quick-start.md): Start building with Solid quickly. Try the playground, create projects with templates, and get your first Solid app running in minutes.

## Guides

### Styling Components

- [CSS modules](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/styling-components/css-modules.md): Use CSS Modules in Solid for locally scoped styles, preventing global conflicts and ensuring component style encapsulation.
- [LESS](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/styling-components/less.md): Integrate LESS preprocessor in Solid apps for variables, mixins, and programmatic CSS features to write cleaner stylesheets.
- [Macaron](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/styling-components/macaron.md): Style Solid components with Macaron's compile-time CSS-in-JS, offering type-safe styled components and variant-based styling.
- [SASS](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/styling-components/sass.md): Configure SASS/SCSS in Solid projects for advanced CSS preprocessing with variables, nesting, mixins, and modular stylesheets.
- [Tailwind CSS v3](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/styling-components/tailwind-v3.md): Set up Tailwind CSS v3 in Solid apps for utility-first styling, rapid development, and consistent responsive design patterns.
- [Tailwind CSS](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/styling-components/tailwind.md): Set up Tailwind CSS v4 in your Solid app for utility-first styling. Configure PostCSS, import styles, and build responsive UIs efficiently.
- [UnoCSS](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/styling-components/uno.md): Integrate UnoCSS with Solid for on-demand utility CSS. Configure Vite plugin, import styles, and create efficient atomic CSS designs quickly.
- [Styling your components](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/styling-your-components.md): Explore Solid's flexible styling options: CSS preprocessors, CSS Modules, CSS-in-JS, and utility frameworks for component styling needs.

### Deployment Options

- [AWS via Flightcontrol](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/deployment-options/aws-via-flightcontrol.md): Deploy Solid apps to AWS with Flightcontrol's automated platform featuring GitHub integration and continuous deployment.
- [AWS via SST](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/deployment-options/aws-via-sst.md): Deploy SolidStart apps to AWS Lambda or containers using SST framework with streamlined configuration and deployment.
- [Cloudflare](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/deployment-options/cloudflare.md): Deploy Solid apps to Cloudflare Pages for fast, global edge hosting with built-in CDN and simple Git integration setup.
- [Firebase](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/deployment-options/firebase.md): Host your Solid application on Firebase with Google's infrastructure for reliable static site hosting and easy deployment.
- [Netlify](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/deployment-options/netlify.md): Deploy Solid apps to Netlify with automatic builds from Git, instant rollbacks, and powerful deployment features included.
- [Railway](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/deployment-options/railway.md): Deploy Solid projects to Railway platform with GitHub integration, custom domains, and straightforward deployment process.
- [Stormkit](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/deployment-options/stormkit.md): Deploy Solid apps as static sites or SPAs on Stormkit with serverless functions support and Git provider integration.
- [Vercel](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/deployment-options/vercel.md): Deploy SolidStart apps to Vercel with automatic builds, serverless functions, and GitHub integration for seamless production hosting.
- [Zerops](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/deployment-options/zerops.md): Deploy SolidStart apps to Zerops cloud platform with support for both static sites and SSR Node.js applications in production.
- [State management](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/state-management.md): Learn Solid's state management with signals, derived values, memos, and effects for reactive data flow and component updates.
- [Routing & navigation](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/routing-and-navigation.md): Implement client-side routing in Solid apps with dynamic routes, nested layouts, route parameters, and lazy-loaded components.
- [Complex state management](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/complex-state-management.md): Master complex state management in Solid using stores and context to build scalable, maintainable applications efficiently.
- [Fetching data](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/fetching-data.md): Master data fetching in Solid with createResource for async operations, loading states, error handling, and Suspense boundaries.
- [Testing](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/testing.md): Test Solid apps with Vitest and Testing Library. Write component tests, simulate user interactions, and ensure code quality effectively.
- [Deploy your app](https://docs.solidjs.com/guides/deploying-your-app.md): Deploy your Solid application to popular hosting platforms including Cloudflare, Vercel, Netlify, AWS, and more with guides.

## Configuration

- [Environment variables](https://docs.solidjs.com/configuration/environment-variables.md): Configure public and private environment variables in Solid apps using Vite's built-in support for secure configuration.
- [TypeScript](https://docs.solidjs.com/configuration/typescript.md): Learn to configure TypeScript with SolidJS for enhanced type safety, better IDE support, and reliable component development.

## Reference

### Basic Reactivity

- [createEffect](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/basic-reactivity/create-effect.md): Learn how to use createEffect to run side effects when reactive dependencies change. Perfect for DOM manipulation and external library integration.
- [createMemo](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/basic-reactivity/create-memo.md): Use createMemo to efficiently compute and cache derived values. Prevent expensive recalculations and optimize your Solid.js application's performance.
- [createResource](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/basic-reactivity/create-resource.md): Fetch async data with createResource. Handles loading states, errors, and integrates with Suspense for seamless data fetching in Solid.js applications.
- [createSignal](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/basic-reactivity/create-signal.md): Create reactive state with createSignal, Solid's fundamental primitive. Track values that change over time and automatically update your UI when they do.

### Component Apis

- [children](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/component-apis/children.md): Resolve a component's `children` prop into a stable accessor.
- [createContext](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/component-apis/create-context.md): Create a context object with a `Provider` component and a default value.
- [createUniqueId](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/component-apis/create-unique-id.md): Generate a unique string for the current render or hydration context.
- [lazy](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/component-apis/lazy.md): Create a component that loads its module lazily from a dynamic import.
- [useContext](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/component-apis/use-context.md): Read the current value of a context object created by `createContext`.

### Components

- [createDynamic](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/components/create-dynamic.md): Render a component or intrinsic element selected at runtime from an accessor.
- [<Dynamic>](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/components/dynamic.md): Render a component or intrinsic element selected at runtime.
- [<ErrorBoundary>](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/components/error-boundary.md): Catch errors thrown while rendering or updating a subtree and render fallback content.
- [<For>](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/components/for.md): Render a list by item identity with a child function that receives the item and an index accessor.
- [<Index>](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/components/index-component.md): Render a list by index with a child function that receives an item accessor and a numeric index.
- [<NoHydration>](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/components/no-hydration.md): Render children during server rendering and skip hydration for that subtree on the client.
- [<Portal>](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/components/portal.md): Render children into a DOM node outside the parent DOM hierarchy.
- [<Show>](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/components/show.md): Render children when a condition is truthy, with optional fallback content and keyed behavior.
- [<SuspenseList>](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/components/suspense-list.md): Coordinate how multiple suspense boundaries reveal their content.
- [<Suspense>](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/components/suspense.md): Render fallback content while suspense-tracked async dependencies under the boundary are pending.
- [<Switch> / <Match>](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/components/switch-and-match.md): Render the first matching branch from a set of mutually exclusive conditions.

### Jsx Attributes

- [attr:*](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/jsx-attributes/attr.md): Force a JSX key to be written as an attribute instead of a property.
- [bool:*](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/jsx-attributes/bool.md): Control whether an attribute is present by writing through `bool:*`.
- [classList](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/jsx-attributes/classlist.md): Toggle element classes from an object of class names and boolean values.
- [innerHTML](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/jsx-attributes/innerhtml.md): Set an element's `innerHTML` property from JSX.
- [on:*](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/jsx-attributes/on.md): Attach an event listener directly to an element with `addEventListener`.
- [on*](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/jsx-attributes/on_.md): Attach an event handler with Solid's delegated event system when the event is supported.
- [@once](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/jsx-attributes/once.md): Mark a JSX expression as static at compile time.
- [prop:*](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/jsx-attributes/prop.md): Force a JSX key to be written as a DOM property instead of an attribute.
- [ref](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/jsx-attributes/ref.md): Capture a rendered element or forwarded component ref.
- [style](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/jsx-attributes/style.md): Set inline styles with a CSS string or an object of property names and values.
- [textContent](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/jsx-attributes/textcontent.md): Set an element's `textContent` property from JSX with plain text content.
- [use:*](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/jsx-attributes/use.md): Attach a directive function to a native element with `use:*`.

### Lifecycle

- [onCleanup](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/lifecycle/on-cleanup.md): Register a cleanup function on the current reactive scope. The cleanup runs when the scope is disposed or refreshed.
- [onMount](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/lifecycle/on-mount.md): Register a function that runs once after the initial render of the current component or root.

### Reactive Utilities

- [batch](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/batch.md): Group reactive updates so downstream computations run after the batch completes.
- [catchError](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/catch-error.md): Establish an error boundary for work performed inside the provided function.
- [createRoot](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/create-root.md): Create non-tracked owner scopes in SolidJS for manual memory management. Essential for nested tracking scopes and preventing auto-disposal.
- [from](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/from.md): Convert an external producer or subscribable into a Solid accessor.
- [getOwner](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/get-owner.md): Return the owner for the currently executing reactive scope.
- [indexArray](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/index-array.md): Reactively map an array by index and return an accessor for the mapped result.
- [mapArray](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/map-array.md): Reactively map an array by item identity and return an accessor for the mapped result.
- [mergeProps](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/merge-props.md): Merge multiple prop sources into a single object while preserving reactive property access.
- [observable](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/observable.md): Convert a Solid accessor into an Observable-compatible object.
- [on](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/on-util.md): Control effect dependencies explicitly with SolidJS's on utility. Define when effects run and manage tracking behavior for precise reactivity.
- [runWithOwner](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/run-with-owner.md): Execute a function under the provided owner.
- [splitProps](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/split-props.md): Split a reactive props object into multiple reactive subsets and a remainder object.
- [startTransition](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/start-transition.md): Start a transition and return a promise that resolves when the transition completes.
- [untrack](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/untrack.md): Execute a function without collecting dependencies from the current reactive scope.
- [useTransition](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/reactive-utilities/use-transition.md): Return a pending-state accessor and a function that starts a transition.

### Rendering

- [DEV](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/rendering/dev.md): Read the development-only `DEV` export from `solid-js`.
- [hydrate](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/rendering/hydrate.md): Hydrate server-rendered HTML and attach Solid's client-side behavior to an existing DOM subtree.
- [hydrationScript](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/rendering/hydration-script.md): Generate the SSR hydration bootstrap script with `HydrationScript` or `generateHydrationScript`.
- [isDev](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/rendering/is-dev.md): Read the boolean that indicates whether the imported `solid-js/web` bundle is the development browser bundle.
- [isServer](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/rendering/is-server.md): Read whether the current `solid-js/web` bundle is the server bundle.
- [renderToStream](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/rendering/render-to-stream.md): Stream server-rendered HTML and continue writing async content as it resolves.
- [renderToStringAsync](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/rendering/render-to-string-async.md): Render HTML to a string after async suspense boundaries settle.
- [renderToString](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/rendering/render-to-string.md): Render HTML to a string synchronously on the server.
- [render](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/rendering/render.md): Mount a Solid root into a DOM node in the browser.

### Secondary Primitives

- [createComputed](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/secondary-primitives/create-computed.md): Create an immediate reactive computation that runs synchronously when created and whenever its dependencies change.
- [createDeferred](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/secondary-primitives/create-deferred.md): Create a deferred accessor whose updates are scheduled for later execution or when the timeout is reached.
- [createReaction](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/secondary-primitives/create-reaction.md): Create a reaction that runs once when the tracked expression is invalidated.
- [createRenderEffect](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/secondary-primitives/create-render-effect.md): Create a reactive computation that runs immediately during the render phase.
- [createSelector](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/secondary-primitives/create-selector.md): Create a keyed boolean accessor that reports whether a key matches the current source value.

### Server Utilities

- [getRequestEvent](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/server-utilities/get-request-event.md): Read the current request event from `solid-js/web`.

### Store Utilities

- [createMutable](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/store-utilities/create-mutable.md): Create a mutable store proxy.
- [createStore](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/store-utilities/create-store.md): Create a reactive store and a setter function for structured state.
- [modifyMutable](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/store-utilities/modify-mutable.md): Apply a modifier to a mutable store inside a batch.
- [produce](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/store-utilities/produce.md): Create a store modifier that applies changes by mutating the current state through a helper proxy.
- [reconcile](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/store-utilities/reconcile.md): Create a store modifier that reconciles existing state with a new value.
- [unwrap](https://docs.solidjs.com/reference/store-utilities/unwrap.md): Remove store proxy wrapping from a store or store subtree.
